site.bio: I'm Saumay Killa, a software developer and AI engineer in New York. I build production web applications and AI systems end to end — from system design and interfaces to backend services, testing, observability, and deployment — using React, TypeScript, Node.js, Python, AWS, and PostgreSQL.

projects.title: Featured Projects
projects.description: Selected software engineering work: AI products, frontend web apps, backend services, and cloud tools.

items.title: Consensus AI
items.subtitle: Meetings with a memory
items.description: A realtime meeting agent that joins the call as CC, listens silently, and interjects when the team reopens a decision already made.
items.longDescription: Consensus AI is a meeting assistant and collaboration platform. CC joins LiveKit rooms as a participant, stays quiet by default, and speaks only when addressed or when Pinecone retrieval shows the topic was already decided. After the call it writes a Gemini summary — decisions, owners, due dates — into SpacetimeDB and indexes the transcript so the next meeting has company memory. The Next.js app covers auth, chat, scheduling, video, and summaries without a REST backend.
highlights: LiveKit agent that listens, then interjects from past-meeting RAG
Gemini realtime voice plus structured summaries after the call
SpacetimeDB for chat, meetings, and summaries — no REST API
learnings: A meeting agent is useful when it stays silent — speak only with retrieved proof.
Realtime voice and company memory are different systems; wire them at shutdown.
If all app state lives in SpacetimeDB, the frontend can subscribe instead of polling.

items.title: Velix
items.subtitle: AI marketing operating system
items.description: A multi-agent marketing platform that turns a website URL into brand analysis, campaigns, personas, and publish-ready social assets.
items.longDescription: Velix replaces a marketing team with LangGraph pipelines on Gemini. Paste a URL and it crawls the site, extracts brand voice and color, then runs Researcher → Persona → Strategy agents with a feedback loop. A second pipeline writes captions, generates images, and uploads assets to Supabase. The frontend is Next.js with workspace switching, Instagram-style preview, and approve/regenerate.
highlights: URL-to-brand profile with crawl, color, and competitor analysis
LangGraph campaign and asset pipelines with a human feedback loop
Multi-workspace auth, storage, and approve/reject UI
learnings: Multi-agent graphs only feel like a product when a human can reject and regenerate a step.
Brand extraction is a retrieval problem first — bad crawl in, generic campaign out.
Workspace isolation is the real multi-tenant problem, not the model call.

items.title: HomeCart
items.subtitle: AR grocery companion for newcomers
items.description: A mobile-first AI companion that helps immigrants decode US grocery aisles with match scores, substitutes, and a live Magic Lens.
items.longDescription: HomeCart is a mobile product for people who just arrived in the US and find grocery stores overwhelming. Onboarding captures home country and language. In-store, Magic Lens uses computer vision to overlay match scores and cooking tips on products. Search in a home language returns US equivalents, quality flags, and lists that export to delivery apps. Built as a mobile-first React Native experience from the Cartographer repo.
highlights: Magic Lens AR overlay with cultural match scores on shelf products
Home-language search with US substitutes and cooking tips
Profile-first onboarding by country and language
learnings: The grocery aisle is a UX problem of translation, not a bigger catalog.
AR only helps if the overlay answers one question: is this the right thing?
Mobile-first means the camera is the search bar.

items.title: Klo
items.subtitle: Voice + camera AI stylist
items.description: An Expo mobile app for live styling sessions — camera, voice, a LiveKit agent, and a RAG knowledge base of fashion documents.
items.longDescription: Klo is a React Native / Expo client for realtime styling. Camera and microphone feed a LiveKit agent so a session feels like a call with a stylist, not a chatbot. A Python stylist-agent runs on LiveKit; KnowledgeIngestor chunks PDFs, embeds them with Gemini, and stores vectors in Supabase for retrieval during the session. Auth, image picker, and secure storage sit on the device.
highlights: LiveKit voice and camera sessions from a React Native client
Stylist agent with RAG over ingested fashion documents
Expo auth, image picker, and secure session storage
learnings: Voice agents fail on mobile when audio session and WebRTC config are an afterthought.
A stylist is only as good as the documents you ingest — RAG is the product.
Realtime UI state on device has to survive backgrounding and flaky networks.

items.title: Outreach Agent
items.subtitle: Research, personalize, draft, send
items.description: An agentic outreach pipeline that researches a lead, personalizes a message, and drafts send-ready sequences instead of generic templates.
items.longDescription: Outreach Agent is an AI pipeline for outbound that does not start with a blank email. Agents research the person and company, pull a hook from public context, and draft a sequence you can edit before send. It sits in the same agentic stack I use elsewhere — structured steps, a human in the loop, and no spray-and-pray copy.
highlights: Lead research before a single sentence is written
Personalized drafts instead of mail-merge templates
Human approval between draft and send
learnings: Outreach quality is a research problem; the model is the last mile.
A four-step graph beats one giant prompt when you need to debug a bad email.
If a human cannot edit the draft, nobody will trust the agent.

items.title: Resume Studio
items.subtitle: ATS-aware resumes and cover letters
items.description: An AI microservice plus Next.js app that tailors resumes and cover letters to a job description and exports PDFs.
items.longDescription: Resume Studio is the JobsHush writing engine: paste a job description, score keyword overlap, rewrite bullets, and export PDF or DOCX. The generator is a Python service (FastAPI, reportlab, python-docx) containerized for AWS Lambda. The frontend is a Next.js workspace with live preview, auth, and cloud storage so a tailored packet is one click from a posting.
highlights: Job-description scoring and ATS-aware rewrites
PDF and DOCX export from a Lambda-ready Python service
Next.js live preview and document workspace
learnings: Users trust generated copy when every line is editable before export.
Document generation belongs on the server; browsers are a poor print engine.
Keyword overlap is a simple eval that makes a black-box LLM inspectable.

items.title: Live Ticker
items.subtitle: Realtime crypto price dashboard
items.description: A full-stack trading dashboard that scrapes live prices with Playwright and keeps multiple tickers updating without thrashing the UI.
items.longDescription: Live Trading Ticker is a React + TypeScript frontend with a Node/Express backend. Playwright scrapes live cryptocurrency prices; the UI charts, filters, and refreshes several tickers at once. Ingestion is isolated from rendering so a flaky source does not freeze the dashboard. Built as a pnpm workspace with protobuf contracts between client and server.
highlights: Playwright-powered live price ingestion
Multi-ticker charts with continuous refresh
Client/server contracts in a pnpm workspace
learnings: High-frequency UI is a rendering budget — update dirty rows, not the whole page.
Scraping is brittle; isolate ingestion so the dashboard survives a source blip.
Typed contracts between scraper and UI prevent silent schema drift.

items.title: Trending Movies
items.subtitle: Discover what's moving right now
items.description: A movie discovery web app with trending lists, search, ratings, and favorites on top of live TMDB data.
items.longDescription: Trending Movies is a TypeScript frontend that pulls live charts from The Movie Database. Browse trending titles, search by name or genre, open details and ratings, and save favorites. The UI is built around fast cards and filters so discovery feels like a product, not an API demo.
highlights: Live trending lists and search from TMDB
Genre, year, and rating filters
Favorites that persist across sessions
learnings: A discovery feed lives or dies on image performance and empty states.
Third-party APIs need a thin client so the UI can mock, cache, and fail softly.
Filters should feel instant even when the catalog is remote.

items.title: RAG Ingestor
items.subtitle: PDFs in, grounded answers out
items.description: A Python ingest pipeline that loads documents, chunks them, embeds with Gemini, and writes a vector store for retrieval.
items.longDescription: RAG Ingestor is the document side of my agent stack. One path loads PDFs, splits with overlap, rotates Gemini embedding keys, and upserts into Supabase pgvector. Another path runs a LangChain RAG loop against Pinecone or FAISS for question answering with citations. The point is a repeatable ingest job, not a notebook that only works once.
highlights: PDF load → chunk → Gemini embed → Supabase vector store
LangChain retrieval with Pinecone or FAISS fallbacks
Batch ingest with API-key rotation for long document sets
learnings: Chunk boundaries matter more than the embedding model for retrieval quality.
Ingest has to be idempotent or you will double-index every retry.
A vector table is infrastructure — treat it like a migration, not a side effect.

items.title: AWS Eventflow
items.subtitle: S3 → SQS → Lambda, as code
items.description: Terraform for a serverless file pipeline: upload to S3, enqueue on SQS, process with Lambda, recover on a DLQ.
items.longDescription: A 100% HCL Terraform stack that wires S3 event notifications to SQS, a Lambda consumer, IAM, and ECR. Files land in a bucket, messages buffer on the queue, Lambda processes them, and failures go to a dead-letter queue instead of disappearing. One apply stands the path up; one destroy tears it down. No console clicking.
highlights: S3 events → SQS buffer → Lambda worker in Terraform
IAM, ECR, and queue wiring checked into git
Dead-letter path for failed processing
learnings: If it is not in Terraform, it does not exist — console setup is a liability.
SQS is the retry layer; Lambda should stay a pure worker.
DLQs are how you debug production async work.
